obligations.statement: The frozen evalBinary and solutionSet definitions represent ordered integral solutions of F(x,y)=m.
The Lean hypotheses encode a degree-n homogeneous integral binary form, rational irreducibility, n >= 3, and m != 0 without an omitted side condition.
Solutions with y = 0 form a finite set and are separated from the rational-approximation branch.
For a solution, g=gcd(x,y) has g^n dividing m; only finitely many scale factors g can occur because m != 0.
After division by an admissible common factor, reduce to primitive coprime pairs and the corresponding nonzero right-hand sides.
Dehomogenize F to f(X)=F(X,1), preserving degree n and irreducibility over Q in the normalized branch.
Choose the finite complex root family of f and record algebraicity, degree, separation, and nonrationality of every root used later.
Factorization and root separation imply that every sufficiently large primitive solution is close to at least one root alpha of f.
For the selected alpha, derive |x/y-alpha| <= C(F,m)/|y|^n with constants independent of the solution.
Choose a real exponent mu with 2 < mu < n and absorb the fixed constant so all sufficiently large solutions satisfy |x/y-alpha| < 1/|y|^mu.
Thue's algebraic approximation theorem: for algebraic irrational alpha and mu>2, only finitely many reduced rationals p/q satisfy |alpha-p/q| < 1/q^mu.
The solutions excluded by the large-denominator estimate, including bounded |y|, form a finite set.
For each root alpha, the large primitive solutions inject into or have finite fibers over the finite exceptional rational approximants.
The primitive solutions for each admissible nonzero right-hand side are finite after merging bounded and approximation branches.
A finite union over common factors, right-hand sides, and roots yields finiteness of solutionSet F m.
The exact root proof has a checked declaration-dependency, axiom, placeholder, unsafe, and oracle report under the selected profiles.
